facts.title: India’s constitutional ideals
facts.copy: The Preamble describes India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic and sets out justice, liberty, equality and fraternity as ideals.

facts.title: Where fundamental rights appear
facts.copy: The Constitution’s Part III sets out fundamental rights, including equality before the law and specified freedoms, subject to the Constitution’s provisions.

facts.title: India’s Parliament
facts.copy: The Union Parliament consists of the President and two Houses: the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

facts.title: Who supervises elections?
facts.copy: Article 324 vests the Election Commission with the superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, State legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.

facts.title: Why Earth has seasons
facts.copy: Earth’s axial tilt changes the angle and duration of sunlight received by each hemisphere during the year; distance from the Sun is not the main cause of the seasons.
facts.sourceTitle: What Causes the Seasons? — NASA Space Place

facts.title: How fast do tectonic plates move?
facts.copy: Many tectonic plates move at rates comparable to how quickly fingernails grow, although rates and directions differ. GPS can measure crustal motion precisely.
facts.sourceTitle: USGS FAQ: How fast do tectonic plates move?

facts.title: Turning sunlight into electricity
facts.copy: A photovoltaic cell absorbs sunlight in a semiconductor; the energy frees charge carriers that can flow through an external circuit as electric current.
facts.sourceTitle: Solar Photovoltaic Cell Basics — U.S. Department of Energy

facts.title: The ocean and atmospheric carbon dioxide
facts.copy: The ocean absorbs a substantial share of carbon dioxide released to the atmosphere. Dissolved carbon dioxide changes seawater chemistry and lowers pH.

facts.title: How much of Earth is ocean?
facts.copy: Oceans cover about 71% of Earth’s surface and contain about 96.5% of all Earth’s water.
facts.sourceTitle: How Much Water is There on Earth? — USGS

facts.title: Where most freshwater is frozen
facts.copy: About 68.7% of Earth’s freshwater is stored in ice caps, glaciers and permanent snow, rather than in rivers and lakes.
facts.sourceTitle: How Much Water is There on Earth? — USGS

facts.title: Tectonic plates are always moving
facts.copy: Plate speeds range from less than 1 to more than 15 centimetres a year, depending on the plate and location.
facts.sourceTitle: Using the Diagram to Discuss How Plate Tectonics Works — USGS

facts.title: What drives the water cycle?
facts.copy: Energy from the Sun and the force of gravity power the continuous movement of water through Earth’s atmosphere, surface and underground stores.

facts.title: A landmark heritage convention
facts.copy: UNESCO adopted the World Heritage Convention on 16 November 1972. It brings cultural-property protection and nature conservation together in one framework.

facts.title: Intangible heritage is living heritage
facts.copy: UNESCO’s 2003 convention describes intangible cultural heritage as community-recognised practices, knowledge and skills passed between generations and continually recreated by communities.
facts.sourceTitle: Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage — UNESCO

facts.title: Five broad forms of living heritage
facts.copy: UNESCO’s 2003 convention identifies oral traditions, performing arts, social practices and festivals, knowledge about nature and the universe, and traditional craftsmanship.
facts.sourceTitle: Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage — UNESCO

facts.title: Preserving documentary heritage
facts.copy: UNESCO’s Memory of the World Programme works to preserve documentary heritage and encourage universal access to it.

facts.title: The United Nations began in 1945
facts.copy: Founded in 1945, the United Nations currently has 193 Member States.

facts.title: What the WTO does
facts.copy: The World Trade Organization provides a framework of trade rules and a forum for its members to address trade matters and disputes.

facts.title: Inflation measures price increases
facts.copy: Inflation is the rate at which prices rise over time. Consumer-price inflation tracks price changes in a basket of commonly purchased goods and services.
facts.sourceTitle: Inflation: Prices on the Rise — IMF

facts.title: The Sustainable Development Goals
facts.copy: In 2015, all UN Member States adopted the 2030 Agenda, which places 17 Sustainable Development Goals at its centre.

facts.title: How long is an Olympiad?
facts.copy: The International Olympic Committee calls the four-year interval between Olympic Games an Olympiad.
facts.sourceTitle: Why are the Olympic Games held every four years? — IOC

facts.title: What the Olympic rings symbolise
facts.copy: The five interlocking rings represent the union of the five continents and athletes from around the world gathering at the Olympic Games.

facts.title: Olympic values
facts.copy: The Olympic Movement identifies excellence, respect and friendship as its three core values.

facts.title: The modern Olympic Games
facts.copy: The International Olympic Committee was founded in Paris in 1894; the first modern Olympic Games took place in Athens in 1896.
facts.sourceTitle: Why are the Olympic Games held every four years? — IOC

currentAffairs.title: IMF publishes its October 2026 world outlook
currentAffairs.summary: The IMF projects global growth at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, with global headline inflation at 4.7% in 2026 before easing to 4.1% in 2027. These are forecasts, not final measured outcomes; the report notes risks including conflict escalation and renewed trade tensions.

currentAffairs.title: NASA reports Antarctica’s third-lowest recorded sea-ice maximum
currentAffairs.summary: NASA reports that Antarctic sea ice reached an estimated annual maximum of 17.59 million square kilometres on 14 September 2026. It was the third-lowest maximum in the satellite record; satellite observations help researchers monitor ice over large areas.
currentAffairs.sourceTitle: Antarctic Sea Ice Grows to Its 2026 Maximum — NASA

currentAffairs.title: WMO reports a strengthening El Niño outlook
currentAffairs.summary: The WMO’s October outlook forecasts further strengthening of El Niño, with the Niño 3.4 sea-surface-temperature anomaly around +3.7°C for October–December. Seasonal climate predictions describe probabilities and broad patterns, not the exact weather for every place or day.
currentAffairs.sourceTitle: Sea-surface temperatures reflect strengthening El Niño — WMO

currentAffairs.title: NSF announces two cross-disciplinary research challenges
currentAffairs.summary: The U.S. National Science Foundation announced Quantum+X and Synthetic Multicellularity prize competitions. The agency says the challenges are intended to encourage research across fields such as quantum technology, biology and engineering.
currentAffairs.sourceTitle: NSF lays the foundation for the next generation of technologies — NSF

currentAffairs.title: IOC and ASOIF hold a women’s sports-leadership workshop
currentAffairs.summary: An IOC report says more than 40 women from 30 Summer and Winter Olympic sports met in Lausanne from 3–5 October for a workshop focused on strengthening leadership skills and confidence.

currentAffairs.title: Skateboarder Rayssa Leal named Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics ambassador
currentAffairs.summary: The International Olympic Committee named Brazilian skateboarder and two-time Olympic medallist Rayssa Leal a Global Ambassador for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. The role is intended to help introduce young people to the Games and its athletes.
currentAffairs.sourceTitle: Rayssa Leal to inspire next generation as Dakar 2026 Global Ambassador — IOC

currentAffairs.title: United States leads the World Athletics U20 medal table
currentAffairs.summary: The official Oregon 2026 results page lists the United States first with 24 medals, including 12 gold, and Kenya second with 11 medals. Check the event page for the complete medal table and results.
currentAffairs.sourceTitle: World Athletics U20 Championships Oregon 26 — Results

currentAffairs.title: UNESCO inscribes 25 new World Heritage properties
currentAffairs.summary: After its Busan session, UNESCO’s World Heritage Committee inscribed 25 properties: 19 cultural, five natural and one mixed. UNESCO said the list also gained its first inscriptions in Comoros, São Tomé and Príncipe, and South Sudan.
currentAffairs.sourceTitle: UNESCO World Heritage: 25 new sites inscribed — UNESCO

currentAffairs.title: PIB explains a proposed National Honour amendment bill
currentAffairs.summary: A PIB backgrounder describes a Bill proposing to extend Section 3 protections to the National Song, Vande Mataram, as well as the National Anthem. The source describes a Bill/proposal; this learning summary does not assert that it became law.
currentAffairs.sourceTitle: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 — PIB

currentAffairs.title: Azerbaijan hosts the 2026 World Environment Day commemoration
currentAffairs.summary: The United Nations’ 2026 World Environment Day commemoration took place in Baku, Azerbaijan. The global observance brought attention to climate issues and environmental action.
currentAffairs.sourceTitle: World Environment Day 2026 Official Commemoration in Azerbaijan — UN Web TV

currentAffairs.title: NOAA issues its 2026 Atlantic hurricane outlook
currentAffairs.summary: NOAA forecast 8–14 named storms, including 3–6 hurricanes, and assigned a 55% probability to a below-normal season. The outlook is seasonal, not a prediction of where or when a storm will make landfall.
currentAffairs.sourceTitle: NOAA predicts below-normal 2026 Atlantic hurricane season — NOAA
